newsitem.title: USA: Democratic senator backs Republican budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Democratic senator backs Republican budget amendment.

text.p: Democratic Sen. Mary Landrieu announced Tuesday she would vote for a Republican-authored balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution, leaving the outcome of a vote on the issue up to Democrat Robert Torricelli, who will announce his decision Wednesday.

Landrieu told reporters she would vote for the balanced budget amendment, despite reservations, to keep her campaign pledge to voters. She said she would also support Democratic-sponsored changes that would protect the Social Security system. She urged Republicans to vote for those versions.

"Based on many statements made during the campaign on this issue, I will cast a yes vote, but with reservations," the freshman senator from Louisiana said at a news conference. She has said she is concerned that the balanced budget amendment would bar the government from setting up a capital budget for long-term investments and could endanger Social Security benefits.
House Republican leaders hope passage in the Senate would give a boost to the measure. They were forced to postpone a Feb. 26 House vote because of opposition in their own party.

Supporters need to muster a two-thirds majority in both the House and the Senate. The expected vote now stands at 66-33 with Torricelli, of New Jersey, thought to be the only remaining undecided vote.

The amendment would require Washington to balance the budget each year starting in 2002 or within two years of its enactment. If it passes Congress, supporters would have up to seven years to win ratification by 38 of the 50 states.
